turns.merchant: Why was my lavender massage oil disapproved?
turns.reply:
Your product "Hemp Extract Massage Oil, Lavender, 100 ml" (id: HG-040) is disapproved because it mentions 'Hemp Extract', which falls under Google's unapproved pharmaceuticals and supplements policy. According to [CBD and other unapproved substances](https://support.google.com/merchants/answer/6165956), products containing cannabidiol (CBD) or similar unapproved substances are not allowed in Shopping ads or free listings. This is a policy decision, not a data problem, so it cannot be fixed by editing product details.

If you disagree with this decision, you can request a review and select "I disagree with the issue" as described in [Requesting a review or appealing a decision](https://support.google.com/merchants/answer/13585221), but you may only get one chance to disagree before a waiting period starts. This needs a specialist, so I've passed it on. Case number CASE-20261008-163309-c42910. A specialist will review it, and the case already includes everything from this conversation, so you won't need to repeat yourself.

results.title: Product barcode number (GTIN)
results.passage: A GTIN is the barcode number a manufacturer gives a product, such as a UPC in North America or an EAN in Europe. Google recommends sending it for every product that has one.

results.title: Product barcode number (GTIN)
results.passage: Products with a missing or wrong GTIN may get limited visibility. If a product does have a GTIN and you leave it out, the product could be disapproved.

results.title: Product barcode number (GTIN)
results.passage: Valid GTINs are 8, 12, 13 or 14 digits long. Spaces and dashes are ignored. The last digit is a check digit and must be correct, so copy the number exactly from the packaging or from your supplier.

results.title: Product barcode number (GTIN)
results.passage: Only send a GTIN you are sure is right, and never make one up. Numbers starting with 02, 04 or 2 are restricted, and numbers starting with 05, 98 or 99 are coupon numbers, so neither kind is accepted.

results.title: Product barcode number (GTIN)
results.passage: If a product really has no GTIN, such as a store brand or private label item, do not send one. Send the brand and the manufacturer part number (MPN) instead.

results.title: Products that have no barcode (identifier exists)
results.passage: The identifier exists setting tells Google that a product has no unique product identifiers at all: no GTIN, no MPN and no brand.

results.title: Products that have no barcode (identifier exists)
results.passage: Set it to "no" only for products that truly have none, such as custom made goods, handmade or one of a kind items, and vintage or antique items.

results.title: Products that have no barcode (identifier exists)
results.passage: Only use "no" when you are certain. If Google finds evidence that the product does have identifiers, the product gets a warning.

results.title: Price in the feed does not match the website
results.passage: The price you send must match the price shown on the product's page and at checkout, in the same currency. If they differ, Google disapproves the product.

results.title: Price in the feed does not match the website
results.passage: Common causes are a delay between changing the price on your website and updating your product data, a sale price with the wrong dates, or price markup on the page that differs from the price shoppers see.

results.title: Price in the feed does not match the website
results.passage: To fix it, change the price in your product data so it matches the product page exactly, then upload the corrected data. You can edit products one at a time in Merchant Center or download the list of affected products and fix them in bulk.

results.title: Price in the feed does not match the website
results.passage: After the fix, Google's crawler rechecks disapproved products over the next few hours or days. Once the prices match, the product is approved again.

results.title: Price in the feed does not match the website
results.passage: To stop it happening again, update your product data on a regular schedule so prices change in both places at the same time.

results.title: Automatic item updates for price and availability
results.passage: Merchant Center can update some product information automatically, using what it finds on your website. Automatic item updates cover price, sale price, availability and condition.

results.title: Automatic item updates for price and availability
results.passage: It works by reading the structured data (schema.org markup) on your product pages, and other information on the page. If your product data says one thing and the website says another, for example $4 in your data but $3 on the page, the product is updated to match the website. This helps avoid some price and availability mismatches.

results.title: Automatic item updates for price and availability
results.passage: Automatic item updates are on by default. You can turn them on or off under Products, on the Automations tab, by choosing an automation and opening View details.

results.title: Automatic item updates for price and availability

results.title: Automatic item updates for price and availability
results.passage: Updates may also not work if your product pages have no structured data, or the markup is incomplete or incorrect. If a page shows several strikethrough prices, the right one may not be found. For sale prices, check that the sale price effective date and its time zone are correct. Updates can also stop if the number of mismatches becomes too large.

results.title: Availability in the feed does not match the website

results.title: Shipping costs

results.title: Shipping costs

results.title: What happens after you fix a product
results.passage: Product issues only affect the products involved. Account issues affect every product in the account. Product issues are listed on the Needs attention tab under Products, and account issues show in a banner at the top of Merchant Center.

results.title: What happens after you fix a product
results.passage: To fix a product issue, correct the product data and upload it again. Some issues also offer a suggested automatic fix in Merchant Center.

results.title: What happens after you fix a product
results.passage: After you update your products, Google checks them again. These checks usually finish within 24 to 48 hours, and products show as pending while they are reviewed.
